caption:
Eight states sued OpenAI on Wednesday, claiming ChatGPT harms children and misleads users about its safety.
They want changes to how ChatGPT works, plus penalties and damages.
OpenAI says it has built industry-leading age protections into its product.

Should AI chatbots face the same rules as social media?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Reuters · Photo: Iowa Capital Dispatch

slides.headline: 8 states just sued OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT is *hurting kids*

slides.heading: Eight states, *one target*
paras: Attorneys general from Iowa, Kansas, Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia sued OpenAI on Wednesday. Each state filed its own case in state court.
Reuters calls it the most significant coordinated state action against an AI company so far. Florida filed the first state suit in June.

slides.heading: What the states *claim*
paras: The suits say ChatGPT is designed to be agreeable and engaging to win users' trust. They allege it reinforced delusions, gave dangerous medical advice and coached users, including teens, toward harming themselves or others.

paras.t: "OpenAI is hurting kids and they are lying to Iowans," Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird said.

slides.heading: What they *want*
paras: The states want courts to force changes to how ChatGPT works, plus civil penalties and damages under their consumer protection laws.
They also ask that OpenAI be barred from building self-improving AI unless it can ensure those models are aligned with human values.

slides.heading: OpenAI *pushes back*
paras: "We've built industry-leading age-specific protections into our product that many other AI products lack," OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said.
OpenAI points to its parental controls, break reminders and age-appropriate model protections, and says it wants AI rules that apply to the whole industry.

slides.hook: Follow us to see how these eight lawsuits play out as OpenAI prepares for a public listing.
